how_to_apply: Visit https://upsconline.nic.in and complete Account Creation, Universal Registration (to generate a Universal Registration Number, URN), and the Common Application Form (CAF) - these three modules are common to all UPSC recruitments and can be filled anytime.
Fill the fourth, post/vacancy-specific module during the notified application window for this advertisement.
Capture a live photograph as prompted while filling the CAF (in addition to uploading a photograph), ensuring it meets the Commission's photo/signature guidelines.
Sign three times (one below the other) on plain white paper in black ink and upload the scanned signature.

Upload supporting documents for each claim (date of birth, caste, educational qualification, experience, disability, desirable qualification, age relaxation, etc.) separately, in PDF format, in the prescribed proforma where applicable.
Use Aadhaar as your ID document where possible for smoother verification; alternatively use Voter Card/PAN/Passport/Driving Licence.
Review all details carefully - applications cannot be withdrawn, and no correction/alteration/modification is allowed after submission.
Submit the application before the closing date: 02.10.2026 (1800 hrs) for all posts except the Ladakh post, or 09.10.2026 for the Ladakh post.
Take a printout of the finally submitted application for your records - do not send it to UPSC by post; bring it only if called for interview, along with original documents.
important_instructions: A candidate must be a citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee (pre-1962), or a person of Indian origin migrated from specified countries with intent to permanently settle in India - subject to eligibility certificate requirements for the latter categories. The date for determining eligibility in every respect is the closing date for submission of the online application. All correspondence from the Commission will be through the registered email ID only - candidates must furnish a correct, active email address. PwBD candidates can apply for posts identified as "suitable" even if not reserved for them, and will be considered on general standard of merit; reservation/relaxation benefits apply only where the disability is 40% or more. Candidates already in regular Central/State Government service must submit a declaration that they have informed their Head of Office/Department in writing about applying. Furnishing false particulars, suppressing material information, tampering with documents, impersonation, or using unfair means will lead to disqualification and possible debarment from future UPSC examinations/selections and Central Government employment. Candidates called for interview will get Commission's contribution towards travel, restricted to Second/Sleeper Class train fare (Mail/Express), paid via NEFT/bank details submitted at the interview. Mobile phones, pagers, programmable devices, smart watches, cameras, or Bluetooth devices are strictly banned in the examination/interview hall. Face authentication is mandatory for all candidates at the examination venue/interview hall. Canvassing in any form will disqualify a candidate. Government strives for a gender-balanced workforce; women candidates are encouraged to apply.

Desirable: Master's degree in Mass Communication/Journalism/Economics/Statistics/English; experience with publishing software (PageMaker, MS Office, CorelDraw, QuarkXPress, Photoshop). Age: 35 years for UR/EWS; 38 years for OBC; 40 years for SC/ST; further relaxable up to 10 years for PwBD. Contractual employees get a one-time relaxation up to 5 years (subject to conditions). content_sections.heading: UPSC Advt No. 11/2026 Selection Process
content_sections.text: Recruitment is "by Selection" - primarily interview-based. Mere possession of the essential qualification does not entitle a candidate to be called for interview. Where the number of applications is large, UPSC may apply shortlisting criteria: Desirable Qualifications, higher educational qualification, higher/relevant experience, or by holding a Recruitment Test (RT). Minimum level of suitability in interview (out of 100 marks): UR – 50 marks, OBC – 45 marks, SC/ST/PH – 40 marks. Where a Recruitment Test (RT) precedes the interview, candidates must clear the minimum suitability level at both the RT and interview stages. Recruitment Test/Combined Recruitment Test (if held) will ordinarily be conducted at: Ahmedabad, Bhopal, Chennai, Delhi, Dispur (Guwahati), Jaipur, Jammu, Kochi, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Port Blair, Ranchi, and Visakhapatnam (for the Ladakh post: Leh, Kargil, Srinagar, and Delhi). Shortlisted candidates must send self-attested copies of documents/certificates as and when demanded by the Commission. Summoning for interview does not guarantee selection. Appointment orders are issued by the Government after final selection. UPSC may grant higher initial pay to candidates adjudged meritorious in the interview.

faq.question: Q1. What is UPSC Advertisement No. 11/2026?
faq.answer: It is a notice inviting online recruitment applications for direct recruitment by selection to 7 posts across various Central Government Ministries, Departments, NDMC, Govt. of NCT of Delhi, and the UT of Ladakh administration.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are there under UPSC Advt No. 11/2026?
faq.answer: There are 212 vacancies in total across the 7 posts: 4 (Assistant Professor Anatomy), 60 (Assistant Professor General Medicine), 2 (Assistant Editor), 1 (Specialist Anaesthesiology), 1 (Specialist Paediatrics), 140 (Assistant Public Prosecutor), and 4 (Public Law Officer, Ladakh).

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for UPSC Advt No. 11/2026?
faq.answer: The closing date is 02.10.2026 (1800 hrs) for all posts except the Ladakh post, which closes on 09.10.2026.

faq.question: Q4. What is the application fee for UPSC Advt No. 11/2026?
faq.answer: The fee is ₹25, with women, SC, ST, and PwBD candidates exempted from payment.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for these UPSC posts?
faq.answer: Age limits vary by post, ranging from 30 years (Assistant Editor, UR) to 50 years (Specialist Anaesthesiology, ST), with category-wise relaxations up to 10 years for PwBD candidates. Full post-wise details are in the Eligibility section above.

faq.question: Q6. How can I apply online for UPSC Advt No. 11/2026?
faq.answer: Candidates must register on https://upsconline.nic.in, complete the Universal Registration and Common Application Form, then fill the post-specific module during the application window, upload required documents, and submit before the closing date.

faq.question: Q7. What is the selection process for UPSC Advt No. 11/2026?
faq.answer: Selection is by interview, with shortlisting (based on desirable qualifications, higher qualification/experience, or a Recruitment Test) where the number of applications is large. Minimum interview suitability marks are UR-50, OBC-45, SC/ST/PH-40 out of 100.

faq.question: Q8. Is there a written exam for UPSC Advt No. 11/2026 posts?
faq.answer: Not necessarily - recruitment is primarily interview-based. A Recruitment Test (RT) may be held only if the Commission decides it is needed for shortlisting, as per the general instructions in the notification.

faq.question: Q9. Who can apply for the Public Law Officer post in Ladakh?
faq.answer: Only Domiciles of the UT of Ladakh (as defined under the Ladakh Civil Services Decentralization and Recruitment – Grant of Domicile Certificate (Procedure) Rules, 2025) with a Bachelor's degree in Law and 2 years' actual practice at the bar are eligible.

faq.question: Q10. Can PwBD candidates apply for posts not reserved for them?
faq.answer: Yes - PwBD candidates can apply for posts identified as "suitable" for their category even if not reserved, and will be considered on general standard of merit; reservation and relaxation benefits require at least 40% disability.
